# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 64 (Bu-Vb Pc64)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 64. Concealing a grave offense

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 64** (*Duṭṭhulla-sikkhāpada*), located in the Sappāṇakavagga of the Vinaya Piṭaka (Vin IV 127), establishes a rule concerning the concealment of another monk's serious monastic breach [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The rule dictates that a bhikkhu who knowingly conceals another bhikkhu's grave offense (*duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ*) commits a *pācittiya*, an offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral; Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997]. The accompanying word analysis (*padabhājana*) defines a "grave offense" in this context as specifically comprising *pārājika* and *saṅghādisesa* offenses [Hüsken 1997]. Commentators and modern scholars highlight a distinct gender asymmetry in Vinaya jurisprudence: whereas a monk concealing a fault of the highest order incurs only a relatively minor *pācittiya* requiring confession and no formal disciplinary proceedings (*mānatta*), a nun concealing a major offense commits Bhikkhunī Pārājika 2 (*vajjapaṭicchādikā*), which results in complete expulsion from the order [Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997].

SuttaCentral identifies full parallels across the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of various early Buddhist schools, including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Dharmaguptaka lineages (often cataloged as Pācittiya 50, 60, 64, or 74) [SuttaCentral]. In Pali, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 64 and Bhikkhu Parivāra Pācittiya 64 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects Pali-internal text reuse primarily with procedural summaries and sub-commentarial treatises—notably the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā*, *Samuccayakkhandhaka* (Kd 13), and *Mahāsaṅgāma* (Pvr 15)—as well as formulaic overlaps with other Vibhaṅga rules such as Pācittiya 9, 66, and 67 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus also match passages to the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and Tibetan Vinaya commentaries, including the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) and the *Prātimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus]. The text is translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
